clue.text: A large number of handouts ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of handouts are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone notes that plenty of leaflets have been ordered from the printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a verb about buying the handouts, but it signals that the letters of HANDOUTS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten hundred is a figure that counts as big in everyday terms.

clue.text: Search about in tin

indicators.note: in places the letters for about within the symbol for tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A search being made around inside a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' is not CAN here but the element's symbol SN; CA (circa) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To look over something carefully for a particular item is to search it.

clue.text: Export leader taken over? Invest!

indicators.note: over signals that the whole piece is turned around, as if flipped
leader means the opening letter of the word export

parts.note: borne means carried or taken

explanation.surface: A trading company's boss has been ousted in a takeover, and the shout goes up to buy shares.
explanation.walkthrough: E (Export's leader) plus BORNE (taken) makes EBORNE, which 'over' reverses. 'Invest' is the archaic sense of clothing someone in robes of office.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone with office is to dress them in ceremonial robes, which is literally to robe them.

clue.text: Excited swimmer is eating continually

indicators.note: is eating means one piece swallows the other, so the swimmer surrounds the other word

parts.note: a fish is a creature that swims
ever means always or continually

explanation.surface: An excitable swimmer who never stops snacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up and agitated is a figurative use of having a temperature.

clue.text: Sadly Carol joined a cult in summer

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A regretful report that Carol joined a cult during the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CAROL and A CULT are rearranged. 'summer' is not the season but one who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that adds up figures is literally something that does sums.

clue.text: Derive support from article in house that's new

indicators.note: in tells us the article sits within the house piece

parts.note: Leo is one of the zodiac houses or signs
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Advice to gain backing from a piece in a newly built home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is not a building but one of the twelve astrological houses of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on someone for help is to draw backing from them.

clue.text: Composition arranged? No chance!

indicators.note: arranged, a musical word, here means the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A dismissive retort that a musical piece will never be arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NO CHANCE are rearranged; 'arranged' doubles as a musical term to fit the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaconne is a musical work built on a repeated bass line, so a piece of music.

clue.text: Pass by the Spanish church feature

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
an apse is the vaulted recess at a church's east end

explanation.surface: Walking past a feature of a Spanish church.
explanation.definitionFit: Time slipping away is said to go by, the intransitive sense.

clue.text: Times editor's removed

parts.note: eras are periods or times
ed is short for editor, and the 's is read as is joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor at The Times has been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is just ERAS, periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiped out or deleted things have been taken away.

clue.text: Demolish one in lead

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the other word

parts.note: to run an organisation is to lead it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An order to knock down one item made of lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the metal but is the verb, to RUN something.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreck or destroy something utterly is to raze it.

clue.text: Sparkling drink gets fragrance after a little work

indicators.note: after places the drink and fragrance behind the bit of work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a little word for a work
ale is a drink
scent is a fragrance

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink comes with perfume once some work has been done.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent, milky gleam like an opal's is a kind of shimmer or sparkle.

clue.text: Clumsy German, hurt when touring university

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the pain word wraps the letter for university

parts.note: to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: An awkward German student gets injured on a campus tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Socially awkward and lacking grace, from the French word for left-handed.

clue.text: Naval officer briefly has love for humanity

indicators.note: briefly means the rank is cut short to its first few letters

parts.note: a commander is a naval officer
passion is intense love

explanation.surface: A short note that a navy officer feels love for mankind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims COMMANDER to COM. 'humanity' is the quality of kindness, not the human race.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanity in the sense of humane kindness is sympathy for others' suffering.

clue.text: Old Bob and Carol separated by rising ground

indicators.note: separated by means the singing word is split open with the hill inside

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a hill is rising ground

explanation.surface: Two people, Bob and Carol, kept apart by a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob and Carol look like names. A bob was British slang for a shilling, a coin before decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob was the slang name for the pre-1971 British twelve-penny coin.

clue.text: Study foremost field

parts.note: to do a subject, as at school, is to study it
main means chief or foremost

explanation.surface: Research into the leading area of a discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: An area of knowledge or activity is a sphere or realm.

clue.text: Sneak in late

parts.note: late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Instruction to creep in after hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sneak' looks like a verb but is the noun: a telltale.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak is a telltale who reports others to authority.

clue.text: Bill's concerned with old tunic

parts.note: a chit is a bill or note of money owed, the 's read as is
on means about or concerned with

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill is worried about an ancient garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is a CHIT, an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiton was the long garment worn in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Lunatic tore round island for sustenance

parts.note: a nut is slang for a lunatic

indicators.note: round means the ripping word goes around the island letter

parts.note: rent is the past tense of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: A madman charged around an island looking for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lunatic' looks like an anagram signal but is NUT; 'tore' is RENT, the old past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that nourishes the body provides nourishment.

clue.text: Upset students making careless mistake

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: pupils are students

explanation.surface: Pupils get distressed after committing a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or oversight is a minor error caused by inattention.

clue.text: Doctor led fraud? That's appalling!

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: Outrage that a medic was behind a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is a verb meaning to tamper: rearrange LED FRAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something terrible or shocking is dreadful in the sense of awful.

clue.text: Soldier gets support for weapon

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for a gunner or soldier
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: A soldier is backed up with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword.

clue.text: Quarrels about recipe for fish

indicators.note: about means the quarrels word surrounds the letter

parts.note: spats are petty quarrels
R, from Latin recipe, is the abbreviation on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Arguments break out in the kitchen over how to cook fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprats are small herring-like sea fish.

clue.text: Hammer old Bob put on shelf

indicators.note: put on in a down clue means the coin letter sits above the shelf

parts.note: s was the abbreviation for a shilling, slang a bob, in old British money
a ledge is a shelf

explanation.surface: Bob, an old man, is placed on a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: S is short for shilling, the pre-1971 British coin called a bob.
explanation.definitionFit: A sledge is short for a sledgehammer, a heavy two-handed hammer.

clue.text: Pope rash to change punctuation

indicators.note: change means the letters of these three words are reworked

explanation.surface: Reckless of a pontiff to alter how text is punctuated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is part of the fodder, not a link: POPE RASH TO gives the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a punctuation mark showing possession or omission.

clue.text: Caught part of face a blow

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the lip is part of the face

explanation.surface: Someone was caught being struck in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip round the ear is a sharp smack or blow.

clue.text: Tiny bit of nasturtium eaten by shy rabbit

indicators.note: eaten by means the small piece is swallowed inside the shy word

parts.note: coy means shy

indicators.note: tiny bit of means just the opening letter of nasturtium

explanation.surface: A timid rabbit nibbles a small piece of a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Cony is an old name for a rabbit or its fur.

clue.text: Find the solution for fish in river

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Puzzling out where a fish is in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a code or cipher is to work out its meaning.

clue.text: Heathen in Italy often on the fiddle

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An unbeliever living in Italy is frequently cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' is British slang for cheating, but here it means playing the violin: Paganini was the great violin virtuoso.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini, the Italian virtuoso violinist, was constantly playing the fiddle.
